full_text_en:
Wu Caiming, Huang Dongliang, Chen Shiyu, Wu Tianshou — Smuggling, Bribery, and Embezzlement Case

Defendants: Wu Caiming, male, 51 years old, formerly a cadre of Fujian Yuanzhubi (Ballpoint Pen) Factory, employed as the domestic plenipotentiary representative of Hong Kong Wenmao Industrial Co., Ltd. Arrested on November 23, 1985.

Defendant: Huang Dongliang, male, 47 years old, formerly acting General Manager of Xiamen Kaiyuan Shopping Center, Fujian Province. Arrested on November 28, 1985.

Defendant: Chen Shiyu, male, 36 years old, formerly Deputy General Manager of Xiamen Kaiyuan Shopping Center, Fujian Province. Arrested on November 28, 1985.

Defendant: Wu Tianshou, male, 44 years old, formerly Manager of the Trade Department of Xiamen Kaiyuan Shopping Center, Fujian Province. Arrested on November 28, 1985.

The defendants Wu Caiming, Huang Dongliang, Chen Shiyu, and Wu Tianshou were prosecuted by the People's Procuratorate of Kaiyuan District, Xiamen City, Fujian Province, before the Kaiyuan District People's Court on charges of smuggling, bribery, and embezzlement. The court lawfully formed a collegial panel and, after an open trial, found the following facts:

In January 1985, the defendant Wu Caiming, introduced by Cai Wenhui, Chairman of the Board of Hong Kong Wenmao Industrial Co., Ltd., negotiated in Xiamen with Chen Yinglin of Hong Kong Eurasia Industrial Co., Ltd. regarding the import of early-model Sanyo brand VTC-1000 VCRs (video cassette recorders) manufactured in Japan, with Wenmao Industrial Co., Ltd. obtaining a 2% commission. Chen Yinglin informed Wu Caiming that, since China restricted the import of VCRs, they could be converted into video players for import and then restored to VCRs for sale. At the same time, Chen Yinglin commissioned Wu Caiming to collect a sample unit of the Sanyo VTC-1000 VCR that had been brought from Hong Kong and converted into a "Polaris" brand video player. In February 1985, Wu Caiming, together with the converted sample, negotiated with the defendants Huang Dongliang and Chen Shiyu, in the name of Hong Kong Wenmao Industrial Co., Ltd., regarding the import of 1,000 Sanyo VTC-1000 VCRs. During the negotiations, Wu Caiming informed Huang Dongliang and Chen Shiyu that after the "video players" were imported, technicians from the Hong Kong side would be dispatched to convert them back into VCRs for sale. Seeking illegal profits for their unit, Huang Dongliang and Chen Shiyu used the quota for importing 1,000 video players that Kaiyuan Shopping Center had originally obtained approval for, and reached an agreement with Wu Caiming to import VCRs. Subsequently, Huang Dongliang assigned the defendant Wu Tianshou to represent Kaiyuan Shopping Center in signing a contract with Wu Caiming, representing Hong Kong Wenmao Industrial Co., Ltd., for the purchase of 1,000 Japanese-made Sanyo VTC-1000 VCRs (at USD 288 per unit, totaling USD 288,000). To ensure that after import the "video players" could be delivered and sold as VCRs, Wu Caiming issued a "memorandum" as an appendix to the contract, undertaking to dispatch technicians from Hong Kong and provide funds to convert them back into VCRs for delivery to Kaiyuan Shopping Center. On February 28 of that year, Kaiyuan Shopping Center opened an irrevocable letter of credit with the Xiamen Branch of the Bank of China in favor of Hong Kong Wenmao Industrial Co., Ltd. In mid-April, the goods arrived at Xiamen port, and Kaiyuan Shopping Center declared them to Customs as imported "video players." During customs inspection in Xiamen, it was discovered that the packaging boxes of the "video players" had been opened and repackaged, the markings on components had been altered, and internal circuits had been cut. Technical appraisal by Customs confirmed that the batch of "video players" were converted VCRs, and they were lawfully detained for investigation. During the customs investigation, Wu Caiming, Huang Dongliang, and Chen Shiyu conspired to conceal the smuggling and destroyed the "memorandum." After the smuggled goods were detained by Customs, Huang Dongliang not only failed to truthfully report the smuggling to the relevant departments and leaders, but on May 2, arbitrarily decided to remit the payment of USD 288,000 to Hong Kong Eurasia Industrial Co., Ltd., from which Hong Kong Wenmao Industrial Co., Ltd. extracted a 2% commission. On July 5 of that year, Xiamen Customs, pursuant to Article 175 of the Interim Customs Law of the People's Republic of China, decided to confiscate the entire batch of smuggled goods, valued at RMB 4 million. Consequently, due to the smuggling acts of Wu Caiming, Huang Dongliang, and Chen Shiyu, Kaiyuan Shopping Center suffered severe economic losses.

Additionally, between September 1984 and March 1985, Huang Dongliang, Chen Shiyu, and Wu Tianshou, taking advantage of their official positions, accepted bribes from Hong Kong merchants and domestic entities during business negotiations and purchase and sales activities, and embezzled public funds. Among them, Huang Dongliang accepted bribes totaling RMB 1,500, HKD 2,000, and foreign exchange certificates worth RMB 100; Chen Shiyu accepted bribes totaling RMB 2,000, HKD 5,500 (of which HKD 2,000 was returned to Huang Dongliang), and foreign exchange certificates worth RMB 3,000; Wu Tianshou accepted bribes totaling RMB 1,900, HKD 4,000 (which were returned to Huang Dongliang), and foreign exchange certificates worth RMB 100. Furthermore, in February 1985, when Wu Tianshou negotiated with Wang Yalang of Hong Kong Lehua Electric Co., Ltd. regarding the import of 500 Japanese-made Mitsubishi brand air-conditioning dehumidifiers, he agreed with Wang Yalang to increase the price of each unit by HKD 30 from HKD 2,550, totaling an increase of HKD 15,000 as a kickback for Wu Tianshou. Because Wang Yalang failed to receive the funds from the company in time, the kickback was not paid. After the case came to light, Wang Yalang handed over HKD 15,000 to Kaiyuan Shopping Center, and Wu Tianshou's attempted embezzlement was not consummated.

The above facts are confirmed by witness testimony, documentary evidence, physical evidence, expert conclusions, etc. The facts are clear, and the evidence is credible and sufficient.

The Kaiyuan District People's Court held in its judgment:

The defendants Wu Caiming, Huang Dongliang, and Chen Shiyu jointly committed the criminal act, which constitutes joint intentional crime as defined in Article 22 of the Criminal Law of the PRC. Wu Caiming and Huang Dongliang played principal roles in the joint crime; after the case came to light, they conspired to conceal the smuggling and destroyed incriminating evidence. Huang Dongliang also arbitrarily remitted USD 288,000 to the Hong Kong merchant. Pursuant to Article 23 of the Criminal Law, they are principal offenders in the smuggling crime and should be given heavier punishments. Chen Shiyu played a secondary role in the smuggling crime and is an accessory as defined in Article 24 of the Criminal Law, and should be given a lighter punishment compared to the principal offenders. Wu Caiming, as an employee of a domestic enterprise and the domestic plenipotentiary representative of a Hong Kong enterprise, and Huang Dongliang and Chen Shiyu, as state functionaries and direct responsible persons of the enterprise, during business negotiations on imports, knowing that VCRs were a restricted import commodity, in order to seek illegal profits for the Hong Kong merchant and their own enterprise, took advantage of the special zone's preferential policies, colluded with each other, adopted means of falsely declaring the name and specifications of imported goods, evaded customs supervision, avoided customs duties, and smuggled VCRs on a huge scale and with serious circumstances, thereby all committing the crime of smuggling under Article 118 of the Criminal Law. Huang Dongliang, Chen Shiyu, and Wu Tianshou, during purchase and sales business activities with Hong Kong merchants and certain domestic enterprises, took advantage of their official positions to accept bribes, thereby respectively committing the crime of accepting bribes under paragraph 1 of Article 185 of the Criminal Law. Wu Tianshou, during business negotiations with a Hong Kong merchant on imports, adopted means of adding kickbacks to embezzle public funds, thereby committing the crime of embezzlement under Article 155 of the Criminal Law. Huang Dongliang, Chen Shiyu, and Wu Tianshou each committed multiple crimes, and pursuant to Article 64 of the Criminal Law, should be subjected to cumulative punishment for multiple crimes. The illegal gains of Huang Dongliang, Chen Shiyu, and Wu Tianshou shall be recovered in accordance with Article 60 of the Criminal Law. Although the smuggling amount of Wu Caiming, Huang Dongliang, and Chen Shiyu was huge and the circumstances serious, they did not line their own pockets during the smuggling activity. Considering the different roles each defendant played in the crime, Wu Caiming may be given a lighter punishment; as for Huang Dongliang and Chen Shiyu, upon decision of the Judicial Committee and pursuant to Article 59 of the Criminal Law, they may be sentenced to a punishment below the statutory penalty. Wu Tianshou had already carried out the criminal act of embezzlement but failed to achieve it due to reasons beyond his will; pursuant to Article 20 of the Criminal Law, an attempted offender may be given a lighter punishment compared to a completed offender.

The Kaiyuan District People's Court, on July 14, 1987, rendered the following judgment:

The defendant Wu Caiming is convicted of the crime of smuggling and sentenced to three years and six months of fixed-term imprisonment.

The defendant Huang Dongliang is convicted of the crime of smuggling and sentenced to two years and six months of fixed-term imprisonment; convicted of the crime of accepting bribes and sentenced to one year and six months of fixed-term imprisonment; the combined sentence is three years and six months of fixed-term imprisonment.

The defendant Chen Shiyu is convicted of the crime of smuggling and sentenced to two years of fixed-term imprisonment; convicted of the crime of accepting bribes and sentenced to two years of fixed-term imprisonment; the combined sentence is three years and six months of fixed-term imprisonment.

The defendant Wu Tianshou is convicted of the crime of accepting bribes and sentenced to one year and six months of fixed-term imprisonment; convicted of the crime of embezzlement and sentenced to one year and six months of fixed-term imprisonment; the combined sentence is two years and six months of fixed-term imprisonment.

The illegal gains of Huang Dongliang, Chen Shiyu, and Wu Tianshou shall be recovered.

After the first-instance judgment, Wu Caiming appealed to the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court on the grounds that "the import of VCRs was normal trade, not smuggling"; Huang Dongliang and Chen Shiyu appealed on the grounds that "they were not aware" of the smuggling of VCRs; Wu Tianshou appealed on the grounds that "the facts were inaccurate."

The People's Procuratorate of Kaiyuan District, on July 23, 1987, filed a protest with the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court. The grounds were: the defendant Wu Caiming played a principal role in the joint smuggling crime, the smuggling amount reached RMB 4 million, and during detention, he violated prison regulations and showed a poor attitude toward admitting guilt; the Kaiyuan District People's Court's sentence of three years and six months of fixed-term imprisonment for the smuggling crime was manifestly lenient.

The Xiamen Intermediate People's Court, in its second-instance trial, held that the facts determined in the original judgment were clear, the evidence was credible and sufficient, the applicable law was correct, and the trial procedure was lawful; with regard to sentencing, considering the criminal liability of each defendant and the historical circumstances at the time of the case, the punishment was appropriate. The appeal grounds of the appellants Wu Caiming, Huang Dongliang, Chen Shiyu, and Wu Tianshou were all without merit and were not adopted. The original judgment's findings that Wu Caiming, Huang Dongliang, and Chen Shiyu did not line their own pockets during the smuggling activity and that they were given lighter punishments respectively were correct. Wu Caiming and Huang Dongliang both played principal roles in the smuggling crime; Huang Dongliang, after Customs decided to detain the smuggled goods, still remitted USD 288,000 to Hong Kong, causing serious economic losses; Wu Caiming, during detention, violated prison regulations; the original judgment had fully considered these circumstances in sentencing, so the grounds for the protest by the People's Procuratorate of Kaiyuan District could not be established. Accordingly, pursuant to subparagraph (1) of Article 136 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC, on September 11, 1987, the court ruled to dismiss the appeals of Wu Caiming, Huang Dongliang, Chen Shiyu, and Wu Tianshou and the protest of the People's Procuratorate of Kaiyuan District, and affirmed the original judgment.
